chapter: Hollywood, Ken Murray and the Penguin years
title: Billy Berg's Swing Club in January 1943
summary: Opens at Billy Berg's after Benny Carter's big band; movie stars flock in and Ken Murray hears of him.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: From then on, they got me--on January 14, 1943, they opened me at Billy Berg's Swing Club.

Tore it up. We were playing soft and we followed Benny Carter fifteen piece band. He had Buddy Rich, that was when Buddy just went into the navy; Buddy was on bass--I mean on drums. We stayed in Billy Berg's Swing Club for about five weeks. That's when we were broadcasting over mutual network there.
I'd love to have some of those shows.
Oh, I'd love to have some of them. I got some of the most beautiful write-ups about what we were playing. We tore it up.

Opening night, after following Benny Carter with that fifteen piece band, the boss said, my god, you'll have to play louder or something. The second night we were there, Jackie Gleason, who we were working with out in the Queens Terrace, he came in----with one of the most beautiful movie stars you ever saw, I forget--I think
it was Belle Wallace. He came in with her-- She was supposed to be what's his name's girlfriend--Earl--

Yes, it was. She was gorgeous. Anyway, when Jackie Gleason and all that bunch started coming in, the manager, Billy Berg, started saying why didn't I book you guys here before, and we started loading them then with movie stars; Lena Horne, all of them just packed in there.
